infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

properties.areaDesc: Western Uinta Mountains
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 12 at 9:59PM MDT until October 14 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Additional snow accumulations up to 8 to 14 inches,
especially for elevations above 9,000ft.

* WHERE...Western Uinta Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM MDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Winter driving conditions are expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Seasonal roads such as Bald Mountain Pass
remain open at this time and may pose a significant risk to
under-prepared travelers. If traveling along high elevation routes,
be prepared for periods of accumulating road snow.

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 13 at 1:49PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W is currently rated as "Medium" by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center, meaning tropical cyclone development is likely, but
beyond 24 hours. It's currently located west of Ujae near 9.3N
164.4E. It continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of
Kosrae/east-northest of Pohnpei.

Inflow into the developing disturbance will allow for locally heavy
rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per hour rain rates probable
from time to time. Rainfall totals will likely be 2 to 5 inches
tonight through Thursday, with locally higher amounts possible.
Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated
wind gusts to 30 knots are possible with any heavy shower or
thunderstorm that develops.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues. Also keep up to date with the latest
information from your local emergency management agency.

NWSheadline: LOCALLY HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS TONIGHT THROUGH THURSDAY, POSSIBLY LONGER

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 12 at 8:40PM PDT until October 13 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and elevated surf are expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding can be expected
near times of high tide.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is
uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is
possible. The risk for significant damage is very low. There
is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around
7.1 to 7.3 feet on Tuesday morning. A Beach Hazards Statement
may be issued on future shifts to follow the Coastal Flood
Advisory due to minor tidal overflow from continued elevated
tides and surf into at least Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 8:40PM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible across the most
vulnerable locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 7.5 feet are
expected late Tuesday morning. A Beach Hazards Statement may
be issued on future shifts to follow the Coastal Flood
Advisory due to minor tidal overflow from continued elevated
tides and surf into at least Thursday.
